transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I suppose I'm here because things haven't really gotten better. Ever since my friend was... killed. I just have this constant... I don't know, this mix of guilt and anger. Fear, too. It just hasn't eased up the way everyone seemed to think it would.
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities since your friend's death?

I suppose... yes. I go out of my way so I don't have to pass that intersection anymore. And I've stopped signing up for most of the tours I used to do, or the safety meetings. I just... people talk, and the conversations always seem to circle back to what happened there. I really can't bear to listen to it. So it's just easier to stay away.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving the moment your friend was killed?

I suppose... yes. Sometimes. It doesn't take much. Just a crosswalk signal... or the growl of a heavy truck. Even just glancing at a walking-tour map. It... it suddenly puts the whole scene right back in my head. Very sharply. I just... I see my friend stepping off the curb, and I can't stop it.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself when these memories come back?
No... I don't think so. I'm just... there. In my own head. I don't really feel like I'm watching from the outside.
Do you find yourself jumping or startled more easily than you used to, by things like loud noises?
No... not really. I haven't noticed anything like that.
Have you been startled more easily by things like loud noises since your friend's death?
I... well, like I just mentioned, no. I haven't really noticed being jumpy around loud noises. It's... just what I said before.
Do you have trouble falling or staying asleep since your friend's death?
No... my sleep is fine. I haven't really had any issues with that.
Do you ever feel numb or disconnected from the world around you?

I suppose... a little. Sometimes when I'm sitting with people I've known for years at the senior center, I just feel separated from them. It's like... they're all chatting on one side of a window, and I'm on the other. But... I don't know.
Do you find yourself more reactive to unexpected events than you used to be?
No... not really. I think I'm about the same as I've always been. Like I said about the noises earlier, I just... I haven't noticed being more reactive or anything like that.
Do you find yourself often blaming yourself or others for your friend's death?

I... yes, I suppose I do. I just keep thinking... if I had picked a different route that day. Or if I'd pushed harder about avoiding that crossing... maybe she'd still be alive. And then I just... I get so angry at the driver. And the town, really, for even letting it happen. But... yes. I think about that a lot.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

I suppose so. I just... I don't really do much of what I used to. I used to plan out my garden beds, and I'd go quilt with the ladies... do theater outings, book club... but now I just look at the calendar and... I don't know. I just don't feel like going. It's like those things belong to someone else now.
How long have you been feeling this way since your friend's death?
Well... it's been a while. Ever since she was killed on that walking tour. I suppose... that was about two years and three months ago now. It's just been going on since then.
Have you avoided many other activities or places besides the intersection and the tours since your friend's death?

I just... I don't go near that intersection. I go out of my way so I don't have to see it. And... I stopped signing up for the other tours. Or those safety meetings they have. I just... I can't sit there and listen to them talk about it. So I just stay away.
How often do you think about what you could have done differently to prevent your friend's death?

...A lot, I suppose. I just... I keep telling myself that if I had picked a different route that day, or... or pushed harder about that crossing, she might still be alive. And then... I don't know, I just get furious all over again. At the driver, and... the town, for letting it happen. I don't really like to talk about it, but... yes, I think about it.
Have you lost interest in all activities that you used to enjoy?

...I suppose so. I used to keep quite busy. Planning my garden beds... quilting with the ladies. We'd go to theater outings, or... I'd go to my book club. But now... well, I look at those things on the calendar and I just... I feel almost nothing. It's like... like they belong to someone I used to be.
How often do you think about what you could have done differently to prevent your friend's death?
You... you just asked me that. I... I already told you. I think about it a lot. I don't really want to keep going over it.
How often would you say you feel guilty about your friend's death?

...I suppose it's always there. It's just... this constant mix of guilt, and fear, and... anger, I guess. Ever since she was killed. People kept telling me time would make it easier, but... it hasn't. It just hasn't eased up at all.
Would you say the guilt you feel about your friend's death is overwhelming at times?
...I suppose so. Yes. It's... it's a lot to carry.
